key_insight: PaperBanana automates the end-to-end creation of publication-ready academic illustrations by orchestrating specialized agents powered by VLMs and image-generation models, turning figure design into an iterative, agentic pipeline that minimizes human effort.
problem_solved: Generating high-quality, publication-ready figures is a time-consuming bottleneck for AI researchers and autonomous research agents; PaperBanana addresses the gap between draft visual ideas and polished, standards-compliant illustrations.
method: Agentic pipeline that coordinates specialized agents for reference retrieval, content & style planning, image rendering, and iterative refinement.
Leverages state-of-the-art vision-language models (VLMs) and image-generation models to translate scientific intent into polished visual assets.
Iterative feedback loop where rendered images are evaluated and revised to meet publication-quality constraints and stylistic guidelines.
impact: Removes a major manual bottleneck in the research workflow, enabling faster paper production, more consistent visual quality, and improved reproducibility for AI/ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing agents (Retrieve → Plan → Render → Refine) and data flow
Before vs. after examples: raw draft vs. publication-ready figure
Decision tree or GUI mockup of planning and style controls
Metric chart comparing time spent and quality scores with/without PaperBanana
paper_title: PaperBanana: Automating Academic Illustration for AI Scientists
paper_authors: Dawei Zhu, Rui Meng, Yale Song, Xiyu Wei, Sujian Li
